First, the situation: My boyfriend and I are going to LED USA next month, and I booked a hotel room for that night. We live in the same city as the venue, but neither of us wants to drive home after the rave because it's a 30-minute drive and we'll be exhausted. Plus, the hotel is just a 10-minute walk from the venue, so it's convenient for us to stay there. We wanted some time away from home, which makes sense. Now, my friends are from about two hours away. They didn't book a hotel room early because they were hoping to share with someone else, but that fell through. Now, hotel prices are high, so they asked if they could stay in my room and split the cost. I said no because I booked it to chill with my boyfriend and maybe have some alone time. Now they're calling me selfish and saying it's a waste of money for me to spend on the hotel when I could just go home, but they don't have that choice. My boyfriend is leaving the decision up to me since I paid for the room. So, the question is, is it wrong for me not to let them stay? Let me think about the reasons why I said no. I booked the room specifically for me and my boyfriend to have some time together. It's a special night, and I wanted privacy and comfort. Plus, after a rave, we might be tired and just want to relax without any disturbances. On the other hand, my friends are in a tough spot. They didn't plan well, but now they're stuck without a place to stay. They're two hours away, so driving back isn't feasible, especially after a night out. They're asking to share the room, which would save them money and give me some extra cash, but I turned them down. They're calling me selfish, which stings. But I also feel like I have the right to use the room I paid for. It's my space, and I should be able to decide who stays there. Plus, having friends over might interfere with our plans for the night. We might not get the privacy we wanted. I also wonder if I'm being too rigid. Maybe I could have been more flexible. But at the same time, I don't want to compromise my own plans just because others didn't make theirs. It's a balance between being considerate and taking care of my own needs. Another angle is the financial aspect. The hotel is expensive, and they're offering to split the cost. But I already paid for it, so maybe I could have considered letting them stay and getting some money back. But I also don't want to feel like I'm being taken advantage of or that it's an obligation. I also think about the future relationship with these friends. If I say no, they might be upset, but maybe they'll understand eventually. If I say yes, it might strain our relationship if they expect similar favors in the future. In the end, I have to decide what's more important: my own comfort and time with my boyfriend, or helping out my friends who are in a tough spot. It's a tough call, but I think it's okay to prioritize my own needs, especially since I booked the room for a reason.
